config._admission_note: Which seasons admit a new study cohort, and (optionally) a per-season intake size. Replaces the old admit_interval_terms count. Default ['Fall'] = one cohort a year, in Fall (walking the calendar and admitting only on Fall lands cohorts exactly one year apart under any cycle). Add 'Spring' for a second yearly intake; admission_sizes lets a department set a different Spring cohort size (a season absent uses cohort_size). Only MANDATORY seasons may admit -- an optional intersession (Summer) is a scarce bonus pool and never takes in a cohort. Edit in Settings -> Admissions, the Plan Builder, or the Scenario Builder.
config._initial_state_note: 'occupancy' = seats in each course used by students of OTHER programs (e.g. Computer Engineering students in CMPS151 or MATH101) -- a permanent background load subtracted from that course's free seats on every mandatory term (see src/simulator.py::_effective_capacity and CLAUDE.md's Initial-State Model). The CS student body itself is rebuilt from current_students.past_intakes by the Intake Planner. Edit on the Data page. num_incumbent_cohorts still works as an engine knob (defaults to 0 / no incumbents) but is not part of the default plan.
config._optional_terms_note: Fall and Spring are mandatory (the only seasons that advance a student's personal_semester clock / max_terms budget; see CLAUDE.md's Term/Season Model). Summer is an optional intersession: a course must explicitly list 'Summer' in its own offering array to run then, and gets a smaller capacity than its mandatory-term seats -- optional_term_capacity_scale x course.capacity. The cycle is 3 seasons (Fall, Spring, Summer), so one year = 3 terms; admission is driven by admission_terms (default ['Fall']), so cohorts enter yearly in Fall regardless of the cycle length. In the default QU plan, ONLY the 22 non-CS service courses (math/science/english/gen_ed) are offered in Summer -- CS courses are never offered in Summer, matching QU's real schedule. optional_terms_enabled defaults to TRUE here: Summer is on. Turning it off (Settings -> PUT /config) collapses to the legacy 2-season Fall/Spring cycle; admission stays yearly-in-Fall either way since it follows admission_terms, not a term count -- see src/models/semester.py::admission_seasons. (The engine's season model is fully generic: an admin could define any terms_per_year cycle, e.g. add a Winter intersession, entirely from config -- nothing about the season names is hardcoded; see tests/test_optional_terms.py.)
config._registration_tier_note: Seat-priority bands by completed_ch, checked in descending order (registration_tier 0 = registers first). QU's real priority-registration policy; a different institution redefines its own bands here, not in student.py::registration_tier.
config._year_standing_note: Ascending completed-CH cutoffs for the flow chart's Year1->Year2->Year3->Year4 stage nodes. QU's actual 4-year/120-CH bands (30 CH/year); a program with a different total credit-hour count sets its own bands here, not in student.py::curriculum_stage.
config._on_time_note: Semesters-to-graduate cutoff for the on_time_rate metric (finished at/under this counts as 'on time'). QU's standard 4-year/8-semester schedule; a program with a different standard length sets its own value here, not in analytics.py.
config._enrollment_priority_note: Phase-1 desired-enrollment order, tried after retakes (which always come first and are not part of this list). Each tier is {categories: [...], min_ch?: N}; a student's eligible courses are bucketed into the first tier whose categories contains the course's category AND whose min_ch (default 0) the student's completed_ch already meets, then tiers are filled in order up to the load cap. A category absent from every tier, or gated by an unmet min_ch, is simply not enrolled that term. This is QU CS's policy (required courses, then cs_electives once junior-standing CH is reached, then service/gen-ed courses) expressed as data; a different program redefines its own tiers/categories here, not in student.py.
config._dropout_note: Dropout has three causes. PRIMARY (GPA): each term a student with completed_ch >= probation_min_ch and gpa < dropout_gpa_floor leaves with probability base_hazard*(1+(floor-gpa)), doubled (early_multiplier) in their first dropout_early_sem_cutoff semesters. SECONDARY (gateway): failing one course dropout_fails_threshold times drops them with prob dropout_prob_on_repeated_fail. TERTIARY (cumulative delay, opt-in via dropout_delay_hazard_scale, default 0.0 = off): independent of GPA, a student whose completed_ch has fallen behind the pace implied by on_time_terms faces a per-term hazard of dropout_delay_hazard_scale * (credit-hour deficit / total program CH) -- models real students who withdraw once they've fallen far enough behind, rather than passively riding it out to CENSORED at the horizon. Left at 0.0 by default; an admin can opt in per plan. CALIBRATION SCOPE: base_hazard is tuned so aggregate 12-semester graduation lands near the middle of a plausible 50-70% range for a program this length — an internally-chosen target, not fit to external data. The early_multiplier front-loading is a face-validity assumption, not a data fit. UPDATE (post optional-term model): a 30-seed sweep of base_hazard over 0.15-0.21 now moves graduation by 0.78pp (0.7382 -> 0.7304) with dropout/censored moving in opposite directions -- a real, monotone relationship, not the flat dropped<->censored trade found before optional terms existed. This swing is now LARGER than the gateway-capacity sweep's ~0.1pp (see _sections_note) -- the reverse of the original ranking. See docs/project_overview.md for how dropout/GPA mechanics work.
config._planning_note: The Intake Planner (src/intake.py). planning labels the decision being made and how current the data is. current_students.past_intakes (most recent first) rebuilds today's student body the next intake walks into; older years are padded with estimates up to intake_analysis.min_history_years. seat_step rounds seat suggestions up (seats, not sections: sections vary in size and a course can grow by widening them). data_sources tags each input 'qu' (QU data) or 'estimate' so every result says how much it rests on estimates. historical_outcomes (optional, 0..1 rates) powers the calibration check.
config._intake_policy_note: How much harm from seat shortages the department accepts, measured against the same students with unlimited seats. Default 'Balanced': graduation within max_terms may drop at most 2 pts and on-time graduation at most 10 pts. min_grad_rate (0..1, optional) adds an absolute floor.

recommendation.why: At 45 students seat shortages could cost up to 11.0 pts of on-time graduation (limit 10; best estimate 9.5), mainly because CSEL2 runs out of seats.
warnings: In the long run 70 a year is sustainable; the lower number now is because today's students (from past intakes) already crowd the seats.
Some estimates are imprecise; increase the number of seeds for a firmer answer.
Most seat denials at 45 happen in Summer catch-up terms, which extra regular-term seats only partly relieve.
Most inputs are still estimates, so treat this result as illustrative.
3 older intakes were estimated to rebuild today's student body.

calibration.note: Enter historical outcomes to check the model.

result.note: Seats sized from demand at the target intake (rounded up to 5), then checked against the policy limits with real seats. A course can grow by widening its sections or opening a new one. Sections and seats change every semester; re-run when the schedule changes.
